h1: Buri Sriphu Hotel — A 4-Star City Hotel in Central Hat Yai Within Walking Distance of Greenway Market
intro: If you're coming to Hat Yai to eat, shop and roam the night markets, and you want a hotel right in the middle of it all, Buri Sriphu Hotel comes up often in reviews · a 4-star hotel on Sripoovanart Road, a few minutes' walk from Greenway Night Market and Central Festival, with an outdoor pool, fitness centre and a large car park that self-drive guests love · rooms from around ฿1,500/night, with an overall score of 8.9 from hundreds of real guest reviews.

body.html: Buri Sriphu opened in 2012 and positions itself as a mid-size convention hotel in Hat Yai — around 136 rooms with an on-site meeting and event centre · what draws leisure travellers isn't a flashy design, it's the central downtown location on Sripoovanart Road that makes getting around easy · Greenway Night Market, Central Festival and Diana Complex are all within walking distance, which matters a lot if you've come to Hat Yai mainly to eat and shop.

The rooms consistently earn praise for being clean and spacious · plenty of reviews mention rooms that are larger than expected for the price, comfortable beds and well-kept bathrooms · the styling is warm, practical city-hotel rather than bold boutique, but it's tidy and easy to settle into · Superior and Standard rooms suit couples or small families, and there are twin-bed options for groups travelling together.
"The room was very clean, the front desk staff were smiling and helpful, and the night market was just a few minutes' walk away. Great value for what we paid."

Facilities are complete for this class — a saltwater outdoor pool, a hot tub and a fitness centre · there's an in-house restaurant and bar · the point self-drive guests praise most is the large car park with EV charging, something that's hard to find among central Hat Yai hotels where parking is usually tight.

Breakfast is where opinions split a little · many guests say the breakfast buffet is well laid out with a decent range, especially the Thai and Southern Thai local dishes · but some reviews note that when the hotel is full or hosting a seminar group, the choice can feel thinner and dishes take a while to refill · if you're visiting over a long weekend, go down early for the better spread and atmosphere.

One honest note: Buri Sriphu frequently hosts meetings and seminars · when there's a large group in, the lobby and lifts can get busier than usual, and a few reviews mention noise or inconsistent information from some staff · none of it is a deal-breaker, but if you're after pure resort-style quiet, a city convention hotel like this may not be the picture that fits you best.

In short, Buri Sriphu is a sensible pick for travellers doing the eat-shop-explore version of Hat Yai who put location and value first · the overall 8.9 from hundreds of real reviews on Trip.com and Booking.com reflects that most guests leave happy · at a starting rate of around ฿1,500/night for a central 4-star with a pool and car park, it's a hard offer to match in this part of town.

honestSummary: Buri Sriphu Hotel stands out for its central Hat Yai location, value for money and large car park, making it a great fit for travellers who come to explore, eat and shop, and for those driving themselves · it's a city hotel that hosts events regularly, so it doesn't offer resort-style calm — but for the price and what you get, it's a sensible choice for a typical Hat Yai trip.
honestChecks: If you want quiet, resort-style calm — this is a city hotel that hosts seminar groups periodically and the lobby can be busy → a Samila beachfront hotel or an old-town boutique would suit you better.
If you're in Hat Yai mainly for the markets and shopping — this location nails it, walkable to Greenway and Central Festival → book a higher floor to avoid street and corridor noise.
If you're self-driving or travelling as a family — the large car park and EV charging are a genuine advantage → book a twin room or one that takes an extra bed for larger groups.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Buri Sriphu Hotel Hat Yai

faq.q: Where is Buri Sriphu Hotel in Hat Yai, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Buri Sriphu Hotel is at 310 Sripoovanart Road in central Hat Yai · about a 5-minute walk to Greenway Night Market and Diana Complex · around 10 minutes to Central Festival · close to Hat Yai Bus Terminal, and roughly 20 minutes by car from Hat Yai Airport.

faq.q: How much does Buri Sriphu Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,500/night for a Standard Room · Superior and Deluxe rooms run roughly ฿1,800–฿2,200, with a Honeymoon Suite around ฿3,200 · prices vary by season and package, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Buri Sriphu Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers in Hat Yai to explore, eat and shop, and for self-drive guests · the central location is walkable to markets and malls, and the large car park has EV charging · it suits couples, small families and value-focused groups.

faq.q: Does Buri Sriphu Hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes, both · there's a saltwater outdoor pool, a hot tub and a fitness centre · the car park is larger than most central hotels and has EV charging points, a detail self-drive guests often praise in reviews.

faq.q: What is breakfast like at Buri Sriphu Hotel?
faq.a: It's a breakfast buffet with Thai and Southern Thai local dishes · most reviews say it's well done · but when the hotel is full or hosting a seminar group, the choice can feel thinner and dishes take time to refill, so go down early.

faq.q: Is Buri Sriphu Hotel noisy, and which room should I request?
faq.a: Because it hosts events, the lobby and corridors can get busy when large groups are in · we'd suggest asking for a higher floor or a room away from the lifts for a quieter, more restful stay.
